table.html:

understanding.purpose: Show the clinic schedule by time, day and room, including sessions that span time slots or rooms.
understanding.reading: Readers scan down the time column, then across the two days to compare room activity. Merged cells indicate that a session continues across slots or occupies both rooms.
groups: Columns 2 and 3 belong under Monday; columns 4 and 5 belong under Tuesday.
The four room columns play the same scheduling role, although their content lengths differ.
The time column anchors each row and needs only enough width for the time labels.
keep_intact: Room labels and clinic names where possible
may_wrap: The cardiology clinic description and its walk-in note
The staff-training closure notice across its two-column cell

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Give the time label and Physiotherapy their minimum intact widths, while retaining r1A’s allocation for the two long descriptions. Monday Room B keeps exactly enough text width for its longest word.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: Give both Room A columns matching, generous widths and retain a wider Tuesday Room B for its longer description, balancing room comparison with content needs.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Shift 10px toward Monday Room A to test whether the cardiology description gains a more natural wrap, while preserving intact time labels and Physiotherapy.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Move 10px from Monday Room A to Tuesday Room B. Test whether the cardiology text can wrap more evenly while giving the nutrition entry a more comfortable two-line measure.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give Monday Room A another 20px from Tuesday Room B. Test whether this keeps the cardiology time with its preceding text, accepting a taller nutrition entry if needed.

bad.name: r1A
bad.note: Shift space from the short middle columns to the two long descriptions. This preserves enough room for the longest single words while giving the nutrition notice more space than in r0B.
bad.why: The 09:00 row label and both instances of Physiotherapy split mid-word, making the schedule harder to scan.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Give Monday Room A enough additional width to test whether the final time can join the preceding phrase, while keeping Tuesday Room B wider than in r0A.
bad.why: The 09:00 row label and both instances of Physiotherapy split mid-word; the final appointment also occupies three lines.

bad.name: r1C
bad.note: Test a wider Tuesday Room B for the nutrition notice, with a moderately wide cardiology column and compact columns for the short entries.
bad.why: The 09:00 row label and both instances of Physiotherapy split mid-word despite the generous width given to Tuesday Room B.

rationale: r2A keeps times and appointment names intact while giving both long appointment descriptions enough space to wrap comfortably. The two day groups remain easy to distinguish, and the merged clinic cell aligns cleanly with the two time slots it covers. Its final appointment fits on two lines, avoiding the extra height seen in several other candidates.

general: Keep row identifiers and recurring appointment names intact so readers can scan and compare rows quickly.
Allocate width according to content and wrapping needs; columns with the same role need not have equal widths.
Judge merged cells alongside the rows and groups they connect, not in isolation.
specific: The time and Tuesday Room A columns are close to minimum widths needed to avoid splitting 09:00 and Physiotherapy.
Monday Room A and Tuesday Room B need most of the remaining width for their long descriptions.

tradeoffs: r3A gives the final appointment more breathing room, while r2A gives more space to the longer cardiology description. r3B makes the earlier time slots more compact but adds a line to the final appointment.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate, coupled estimates from the rendered candidates, not independently verified thresholds. Changes must be balanced across columns to keep the total at or below 719px; values near a wrapping threshold may change the layout.

critique.good: The equal room widths make the day groups easy to compare. Time labels and headers stay intact, and the merged closure reads clearly across Monday.
critique.problems: The cardiology description breaks into short phrases, while the nutrition notice is also cramped. The short entries in Monday Room B and Tuesday Room A leave comparatively unused space.
critique.cause: All four room columns receive 163px despite having very different content lengths.

critique.good: The wider columns follow the content: cardiology and nutrition have more room, while the shorter room entries still fit. Both day groups remain clearly legible.
critique.problems: The cardiology description leaves 10:30 alone on its last line, and the nutrition notice still takes three lines. The narrow middle columns also make the room grid feel compressed between two wide outer columns.
critique.cause: Monday Room A at 220px falls just short of fitting the final time with the preceding phrase; Tuesday Room B at 207px is still too narrow for a shorter nutrition notice. The 108px and 119px middle columns create the strong width contrast.

critique.good: The room columns have a more moderate rhythm than in r0B, and the day groups, time labels and merged cells remain easy to follow.
critique.problems: The cardiology description separates the doctor's name across lines, while the nutrition notice remains in three lines. Tuesday Room A has noticeably more space than its short entries need.
critique.cause: Monday Room A at 180px is too narrow to keep the doctor’s name together in its current line; Tuesday Room A at 180px takes space that could help either long description.

critique.good: The two longer descriptions have enough space to sit comfortably, and the Monday closure reads as one notice across both rooms. The two day groups are reasonably balanced.
critique.problems: The 09:00 time label breaks after the second digit, and Physiotherapy breaks across lines in both Tuesday slots. These splits disrupt the time anchor and make the repeated clinic harder to scan.
critique.cause: The 64px time column leaves 43px for a 44px label; the 118px Tuesday Room A column leaves 97px for a 98px word.

critique.good: The wider Monday Room A keeps the cardiology description together in two lines, making that merged session easy to read.
critique.problems: The time and Physiotherapy splits remain. The narrower Tuesday Room B forces the nutrition description onto three lines, increasing the final row height and leaving the day groups visually uneven.
critique.cause: The 64px and 118px columns are each 1px too narrow for their longest unbreakable content. Shifting 30px from Tuesday Room B to Monday Room A leaves the nutrition description with only 171px of text width.

critique.good: The wider Tuesday Room B keeps the nutrition description to two lines, and the closure still reads clearly across Monday.
critique.problems: The time and Physiotherapy splits remain. The narrower Monday Room A also breaks the cardiology description into shorter fragments, separating the doctor’s name across lines.
critique.cause: The 64px and 118px columns are each 1px too narrow for their longest unbreakable content. Monday Room A has only 167px of text width, encouraging an earlier wrap in the cardiology description.

critique.good: The time labels and room headers stay intact, and the merged cells clearly show sessions spanning time slots or rooms. The nutrition entry fits in two lines, keeping the final row reasonably compact.
critique.problems: The cardiology entry ends with the isolated time “10:30” on a third line, making its merged cell look bottom-heavy. Monday Room A and Tuesday Room B are much wider than the other room columns, though their longer descriptions justify some difference.
critique.cause: At 205px, Monday Room A has 184px for text, which is insufficient to keep the time with the preceding words. Tuesday Room B's 222px width gives the nutrition entry enough space for two lines.

critique.good: The headers, time labels and individual words remain intact, and the day and room groupings are easy to follow.
critique.problems: The cardiology entry still leaves “10:30” alone, while the nutrition entry gains a third line ending in the isolated word “diabetes”. This makes the last row taller without improving the earlier session.
critique.cause: The extra 10px in Monday Room A does not prevent the cardiology wrap; taking those 10px from Tuesday Room B reduces its text width enough to push “diabetes” onto a new line.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r1A.why: The narrow time column splits 09:00, and Tuesday’s Room A splits Physiotherapy in both rows. Both breaks disrupt scanning.

r2A.why: Times and clinic names stay intact, while the two long entries wrap naturally into three and two lines. The room columns have useful proportions and the rows scan clearly.

ref_auto.why: Times and clinic names remain intact, and the day groups are balanced. The nutrition entry takes three lines, leaving the last row taller than in B.

ref_equal.why: All words and times stay intact, but the oversized time column leaves both long clinic entries in narrow columns. Their four-line wraps make the schedule tall and uneven.

r0C.why: Times and clinic names stay intact, and the long entries wrap naturally. Tuesday’s Room A has more space than its short entries need, while Room B’s nutrition entry takes three lines.

r2B.why: The schedule scans clearly, with intact times and clinic names. The nutrition entry wraps to three lines, while Monday’s Room A has slightly more width than it needs for its current wrapping.

raw.unsure: The images are small, so the precise column boundaries and line breaks are judged visually.

r0C.why: Times and short clinic names remain intact, and the long entries wrap legibly. Monday Room A is somewhat narrow, splitting the doctor's name across lines.

r2A.why: The time labels and clinic names stay intact, while the two long entries wrap naturally. The wider Monday Room A and Tuesday Room B columns reflect their content.

r1A.why: The 09:00 time and both instances of Physiotherapy break within the word or identifier, making the schedule harder to scan.

ref_auto.why: The schedule scans cleanly and keeps names and times intact. The Tuesday Room B entry wraps to three lines, leaving a little more vertical space than B.

r2B.why: The headers and rows are clear, with intact times and clinic names. The long Tuesday Room B entry wraps to three lines, creating a slightly tall final row.

ref_equal.why: The oversized Time column takes space from both long clinic entries, forcing them into four lines each and making the table taller and less balanced.

raw.unsure: D and E are very close in quality; their small width differences have little effect on readability.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
